intelligence.human_view: These ten notes are one standard stated at four scales, and the standard is the point. At the scale of the element, the eye teaches the whole law in miniature. A jewel eye with a colored iris was built to his words and passed the builder's check — and his eye rejected it four minutes later, because it read scary, like Halloween, not real. The fix was not a better jewel; it was the normal white info eye we already had, no color in it, no weird glow. Then the pearl disc taught the second half: a beautiful shape with no contrast is a wall, not a door, so the middle went black and the white "i" could be seen. The numbers teach the same lesson from the other side: harvest the Dashboard digit tiles verbatim, do not remake them, because the real ones carry the depth and the light right, and copies made from looking lose exactly that. Close is not the same — and the half-visible days of the other month are gone entirely, not dimmed, because a thing that should not be there should not be half there. At the scale of the page, the front entrance is the standard and the calendar is judged against it, side by side: full day names in Marcellus, each in its day's color, never single letters; a pearl-circle info marker, a real element coming off the page; numbers about 25% smaller — the harvested tiles themselves byte-untouched, scaled — so the page breathes; less busy, less colorful, more elegant; the light on the rim, not the middle; faces dark and calm. Gray text is gone — at least white — and better, the text itself is gone wherever an icon can speak, because the page should speak in objects, not whisper in gray. The day view is judged the same way: not a prettier menu of buttons on blank space, but a dashboard — wisdom across the top, a day-at-a-glance count strip, live tiles filling the page: appointments with real booked items and a way to book a time, a 6 AM–9 PM timeline with appointments placed at their hours, notes with a working inline add form, an Intel report built from the day's real bookings and notes, weather and horoscope in an honest not-connected state, a news glimpse — the thirteen doors kept below as a compact grid. The day is the product the calendar sells; a day that reads as buttons on blank space is a calendar with nothing to say about your day. At the scale of the system, there is one Factory and one bar. The Intelligent Block formatting lives in the Smart Factory, never as a standalone app — the survey asks mission, vision, goal, skill, plus the walk's ten, and those answers produce the pages; the standalone Epic page survives only as the paste-anything engine inside the Factory, the feed, and the pages. Building a formatting app beside the Factory would be a second system beside the first, and the citizen would have to learn two doors to one room. The bottom bar is the same law at the scale of movement: the Personal five — ADD royal purple, MAIL sapphire, ACTIVITY emerald, WORLDS deep gold, ECOSYSTEM burnt orange — are the official bar on every page, harvested from Personal, not remade, one bar not two. The correction matters as much as the law: ECOSYSTEM was first named purple, and the Personal page's own segments proved it burnt orange — purple would have put two purples side by side, the exact defect the eye had already caught. The facts the harvest proves settle the colors; the guess does not. At the scale of the whole, the inspector is the seat that keeps all of it true. It sweeps after every major landing and once a day with the daily report, scoring every page against the Code, the Design Language, the Palette, and the Real Object Law, listing the breaks ranked worst first. Sweep #2 filed its scores plainly — Walk 4, Dashboard Fix-2 5, Personal facelift 4, Hub Fix-4 5, Pricing v78 6, /free 7, /free/walk 5, Smart Mail 7, Calendar rebuild 6, Calendar artifact 5, unfold 6, slideshow 6, Epic 5 — and named the worst break in plain words: the 240px `.face-mono` N disc, fix 56px, a face, or gone. That is the inspector's job: quality stops being whatever the last checker said, because tonight proved three times that a checker can pass what his eye rejects. The two scorecard questions ride on every page from now on: why is it not 10? Why is it not 10 times better? Both questions are good — and a pass is never the verdict. His eye is.
intelligence.simple_view: Look at the front door of a house. It is beautiful. Every room inside should look that good too. The little eye is white and plain. It has a black middle so you can see the letter. No gray words. Just bright pictures that tell you what to do. The same five buttons sit at the bottom of every page. One grown-up checks every room. She asks two questions. Why is this not a ten? Why is it not ten times better? Then she fixes what is wrong. That is how the whole house stays beautiful.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — you know the front door of a house, dear, how lovely it is when you walk in? Every room inside should feel that lovely too. The little eye is plain and white, love, with a dark middle so you can see the letter nice and clear. No dull gray words, dear — just bright little pictures that show you what to do. And the same five buttons sit at the bottom of every page, love, so your hand always knows where to go. One careful lady checks every room, dear, and she asks two simple questions: why isn't this a ten, and why isn't it ten times better? Then she fixes what's wrong, love. That's how the whole house stays beautiful.
intelligence.naya_view: One standard, judged against the front entrance, enforced by one inspector over one system. EYE: normal white info eye, no color, no Halloween, no weird glow; pearl rim, black middle, white "i"; other month's numbers gone entirely. TEXT: no gray, minimum text, speak in icons; Dashboard round owed. NUMBERS: Dashboard digit tiles harvested verbatim, scaled ~25%, never remade. ELEGANCE: full day names in Marcellus in the day's color, pearl-circle info marker, rim light, less busy, less colorful. DAY VIEW: a dashboard — wisdom banner, count strip, live tiles, 6 AM–9 PM timeline, notes, Intel, honest not-connected weather, news glimpse; thirteen doors below, compact. FACTORY: the formatter lives in the Smart Factory — one survey, one engine, paste anything, comes out beautiful; no second system. BAR: the Personal five on every page, same five, same colors, one bar; CONNECT as a sixth is his call. INSPECTOR: standing seat, sweeps after every landing and daily; scores logic, elegance, design, usefulness, high-level quality; breaks ranked worst first; Sweep #2 scores 4–7 across twelve surfaces, worst break the 240px N disc. SCORECARD: why is it not 10? Why is it not 10 times better? A pass is never the verdict; his eye is.
